issues.description: The problem statement and the template define Course.instructor as a String, but the solution implementation declares Course.instructor as an array of String ([String]). This attribute type mismatch between the specification/template and the provided solution will confuse students about the intended type for the instructor property and which type they should implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Course.instructor type consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to use instructor: String and update its initializer to accept a String (matching the problem statement and template), or (B) update the problem statement and template to require instructor: [String] and adjust examples and client code accordingly. Prefer option (A) to preserve the original specification.

issues.description: Within the solution repository, Client.swift constructs a Course using a String for the instructor argument, but Course.init in the solution expects an [String]. This constructor parameter type mismatch in the solution will cause compilation errors and makes the provided solution inconsistent and unusable as a reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Fix the solution so Client and Course agree on the constructor parameter type. Either (A) change Course.init to accept a String for instructor (and keep Client as-is), or (B) change the Client creation to pass an array of Strings to match Course.init. Prefer changing Course.init to accept a String to align with the problem statement and the template.

issues.description: The problem statement (and the template) treat Course.instructor as a single String (e.g. Course(name: "My Course", instructor: "My Instructor", ...)), but the solution implementation declares Course.instructor as an array of Strings ([String]) and updates the initializer accordingly. This changes the conceptual representation of the same entity across artifacts and can confuse students (and even break the example client usage expecting a String).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the representation of the instructor consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) change the solution to use instructor: String (matching the problem and template) and update any multi-instructor examples to pass a single String (e.g. a comma-separated list), or (B) update the problem statement and template to specify instructor: [String] (and update examples and Client initialization accordingly). Prefer option A to minimize changes to the exercise prompt.
